newsitem.title: CANADA: Petro-Can to announce Terra Nova partner.
newsitem.headline: Petro-Can to announce Terra Nova partner.

text.p: Petro-Canada is expected to name shortly a consortium that would become a strategic alliance partner for the construction and development of the proposed Terra Nova oil project off Canada's east coast.

Three consortia were bidding to be alliance partners for construction of Terra Nova's mode of production. Under the proposed deal, the sucessful bidder would also become operator of a percentage of Petro-Canada's share of oil output, Petro-Canada spokesman Bill Simpkins said on Tuesday.
"It means they will share in the risk and reward, so it will be very different from a traditional contractor relationship," Simpkins said.

Terra Nova, the C$4.2-billion Petro-Canada-operated project located 350 km southeast of Newfoundland, is widely expected to be Canada's second major producing offshore project after Hibernia. Its reserves are estimated at over 400 million barrels.

Partners in the project, which is expected to produce over 100,000 barrels per day for 15 to 18 years starting in 2001, include Petro-Canada, Mobil Corp unit Mobil Oil Canada Ltd, Husky Oil Operations Ltd, Murphy Oil Corp MUR.N and Mosbacher Operating Ltd.
A joint regulatory review of the project is scheduled to start in January and was expected to take nine months to complete.
Simpkins said a decision on whether to give the project the final go-ahead would likely be made in the third quarter of 1997.
